name: Bintsuke wax makeup base

lead: Bintsuke is a wax applied to most of the face and neck before oshiroi, the white makeup worn by geisha, maiko and kabuki performers. It creates a smooth layer for the pigment to sit on.
The look is a flat, bright white face with a deliberate bare patch at the nape.

paras: The wax is spread over the face and neck, then oshiroi mixed with water is brushed on and set with powder; eyes, brows and lips are then painted. A related wax, ishineri, smooths the brows.
Older oshiroi contained white lead; modern products are made without it. Heavy makeup can irritate skin.

chain: Wax smoothed over face and neck
angle.text: The wax provides an even surface so the white powder applies smoothly and gives the traditional bright finish.

lead: Bintsuke is a facial wax used in traditional Japanese stage and geisha makeup as a base applied across most of the face and neck before white oshiroi powder. A related wax, ishineri, is applied to the eyebrows to smooth them for painting.[1]

Oshiroi is mixed with water to a precise consistency and applied with a wide, flat brush, then dusted with rice powder before the eyes, brows and lips are defined.[1] Geisha and maiko traditionally leave part of the nape unpainted (eri-ashi).[1] Historically oshiroi contained white lead, which could cause poisoning.[1]

paras: Bintsuke is applied to the face and neck before oshiroi.[1] Practitioners layer white powder, then add red and black accents around eyes, brows and lips.[1]
White lead in older oshiroi was linked to lead poisoning; Japan is reported to have banned it in cosmetics in 1934.[1]
